_why: OrcaSlicer descends from Bambu Studio; PrusaSlicer and SuperSlicer share a lineage. Measured against the real files, Orca and SuperSlicer share only 13 exact parameter names out of ~90, while SuperSlicer and PrusaSlicer share all 90. So generating PS from SS is close to a copy, and generating Orca needs this table. The tier anchors in source/tier-anchors.json are in ORCA names because they came from a forum table comparing two Orca profiles; this is what lets them drive PS/SS output too.
_confidence: Entries under `mapped` are ones I am confident about. Entries under `unmapped_orca` exist in the anchor table but have no clean PS/SS equivalent, or the equivalent lives at a different scope (filament/printer rather than process). Do not guess these into `mapped` without checking against a real exported profile from each slicer — a wrong mapping is worse than a missing one, because it silently writes a plausible value into the wrong setting.
_scope_note: Some Orca process keys correspond to PS/SS settings that are NOT process-level. retraction and z-hop are printer-level in PS/SS; pressure advance and volumetric caps are filament-level. Those are listed in `scope_differs` and must be emitted into the right section, not the print preset.

z_hop._note: Resolved 2026-09-01: dropped from the print presets entirely and authored as retract_lift on the printer variants, which is the only scope PS/SS read it in. The per-TIER ramp the print presets carried (2x layer height, 0 for Speed) is not expressible anywhere -- retract_lift is printer scope in PS/SS and z_hop is machine scope in Orca, and one printer serves four tiers. The Draft row is the value kept, because Draft is the tier defined as stock.

pressure_advance.note: PS/SS have no native PA field; it is passed to Klipper via filament custom g-code or left to printer.cfg.

default_fan_speed._note: Three names for one setting, all verified against the installed binaries on 2026-09-01: SuperSlicer default_fan_speed, PrusaSlicer min_fan_speed, Orca fan_min_speed. SuperSlicer drops min_fan_speed SILENTLY -- no warning, absent from the G-code footer -- so the wrong name here costs the fan floor with nothing to notice.

_jerk_note: Every *_jerk key is unmapped on purpose. Orca exposes per-feature jerk; PS/SS expose a single machine-level jerk, and on a Klipper machine both are really square-corner velocity. SQV is handled as a tier property passed to START_PRINT rather than as a slicer setting — see source/model.json and docs/STATUS.md. v1.0.2 removed SQV from the bundles precisely because writing it as a slicer field caused PrusaSlicer errors.
_value_vocabularies_differ_too: Mapping key NAMES is not enough: the same key can carry different enum values per slicer. PrusaSlicer 2.9.6 rejected brim_type=auto_brim from the Orca-derived Stock tier and substituted outer_only, with a warning dialog on every launch. Checked the rest of the Stock tier's non-numeric values: seam_position=aligned and fill_pattern=grid are valid in both.

filament_scope._what: PS/SS filament key -> Orca filament key. Separate from `mapped`, which is process scope.
filament_scope._evidence: Names verified against Sovol's shipped Orca filament profiles in Sovol3d/Sovol-OrcaSlicer on GitHub. Where a name was absent there it was checked across the whole OrcaSlicer profile tree by file count: filament_colour 0 files (Orca has no such key -> default_filament_colour, 103), filament_notes 75, filament_shrink 72, compatible_printers_condition 682.

_fan_out._why: Orca has no single bed temperature. It carries one per plate type, and the preset also names which plate it assumes via bed_type. Our presets have a single value, so it is written to all four -- whichever plate the user selects then gets the intended temperature.

_paired._why: Orca ignores pressure_advance unless enable_pressure_advance is also set.

_forced._why: Not translations -- decisions. activate_air_filtration drives the exhaust fan at a fixed duty for the whole print, and on this machine the chamber PI loop owns that fan (notes/kb/mods/exhaust-fan-pid.md). A slicer-issued duty would fight it, so it is forced off regardless of what Sovol ships. activate_chamber_temp_control WAS forced off here and is not any more: it moved to the material bases in presets.json on 2026-09-04, where each material also carries its own chamber_minimal_temperature. Forcing it off meant every material except PLA emitted BARE M191 and took the macro's 22 C minimum and 32 C target fallback -- so ABS shipped a 60 C ceiling in its preset that never reached the printer. The PLA-only override in emit_orca_filament that worked around this is gone with it. An unchecked profile still emits bare M191; an enabled one emits M191 at Orca's exact Minimal followed by M141 at its Target. The generated start contains the ordered M191 itself, which makes Orca suppress its automatic pre-start duplicate. See notes/incidents/2026-08-17-zero2-startup-crash.

_unmapped.bridge_fan_speed: No filament-scope equivalent in Orca. Its nearest relative, internal_bridge_fan_speed, is process scope, so mapping it here would write into the wrong preset type. Dropped deliberately.
_unmapped.compatible_printers: Handled structurally, not by name: Orca wants a JSON list of machine preset names, which the emitter builds.

_roots._why: Orca filament presets inherit a per-material root, and each root itself inherits fdm_filament_common. The whole closure must be shipped AND listed in the vendor index -- an unlisted root is an absent root, which fails the entire vendor. Note PETG inherits fdm_filament_pet, not _petg.

process_forced._why: Not translations -- decisions, and Orca-only concepts with no PS/SS equivalent to translate FROM. Same role as filament_scope._forced. CORRECTED 2026-09-07: gcode_label_objects is PRINT scope in ALL THREE, not printer scope in PS/SS. It lived on the printer preset and PrusaSlicer ignored it there -- a live job resolved it to `disabled` and emitted no EXCLUDE_OBJECT lines, so object skipping never worked in PrusaSlicer either. Prusa's own bundle puts it under [print:*common*]. It is now in *SV Zero General*, and exclude_object stays an Orca-only forced value.
process_forced._skirt_start_angle: Front-right, requested 2026-09-13 to shorten travel from the purge. Orca accepts -180..180 degrees; -45 is equivalent to 315. Dormant when skirt_loops is zero. This sets skirt entry, not model seam placement.

_mapping_provenance_2026_09_07: Sixteen mappings added by DIFFING our keymap against the published PrusaSlicer/SuperSlicer -> OrcaSlicer converters: theophile/SuperSlicer_to_Orca_scripts (328 pairs) and bwees/orca_prusa (211). Their tables and ours DISAGREED ON NOTHING -- every key we already mapped, we mapped the same way -- but they cover keys we simply never reached, because ours grew one bug at a time. The consequences were real: support_material_style=organic never reached Orca, so it used its own `default` support style while PS/SS used organic; top/bottom_fill_pattern=monotonic never reached it either; and skirts=0 did not, so Orca printed a skirt the other two did not. See notes/kb/multi-slicer-prior-art.md.
_expanded_2026_09_07: Grown from 71 to 280 pairs. Sourced by majority vote across three published PrusaSlicer/SuperSlicer -> OrcaSlicer converters (theophile 328 pairs, bwees 211, robertoSreis 22), then filtered on BOTH sides: the PS/SS name must be a real option in ps-known-options.json or ss-known-options.json, and the Orca name must appear in OrcaSlicer's own shipped profiles -- 887 distinct keys harvested from 8,827 files in the installed 2.4.2. The second filter is not optional: the Perl table interleaves conversion-TYPE markers with key names, so an unfiltered import would have added `array`, `single` and `nearest` as Orca options. Pairs where the sources disagree outright are in _ambiguous and deliberately NOT added.\n\nMost of these the Zero does not set today. They are here so the NEXT setting added to the master reaches Orca instead of being silently dropped -- which is how support_material_style=organic went missing for months.

_ambiguous._why: The converters disagree on the Orca name for these. Left unmapped rather than guessed; resolve against Orca's UI before adding.

_percent_to_ratio._why: Orca expresses flow ratios as a plain 0-2 multiplier; PrusaSlicer and SuperSlicer express the same quantity as a percentage. Emitting 100 where Orca wants 1.0 is refused outright: "bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio: 100 not in range [0.000000,2.000000]". Found 2026-09-07 by the slice matrix -- the upstream validator passed the same file, because the value is a valid number and only the SLICER knows the range.

process_omit._why: PS/SS-side keys that are deliberately NOT translated into Orca, because Orca's own default is the better behaviour and ours would override it. The counterpart to process_forced: forced adds what cannot be translated, omit withholds what should not be. Omitted keys stay in `mapped` -- the pair is real and correct, we simply decline to use it here -- so they are NOT counted as unmapped.
process_omit._brim: 2026-09-07. Orca resolves brim_type=auto_brim, which decides per object whether a brim is needed; that is strictly better than a fixed width and the operator asked to leave it alone. PrusaSlicer has no adaptive equivalent (brim_type is on/off at a fixed width) and SuperSlicer's is brim_ears, a different key with different semantics. Sending our PS/SS brim settings to Orca would replace an adaptive decision with a constant.
